ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory onboarding screening of every UBO, director and appointed gérant against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the French national asset-freeze register (Ministère de l'Économie, gels d'avoirs), applicable UN Security Council resolutions implemented via EU regulations, the French PEP definition under Article L.561-10 CMF, and OFAC SDN screening where USD or correspondent clearing rails (Airwallex, Swift, correspondent banks) are used. Continuous adverse-media and PEP re-screening is contractually required at any trigger event: change of ownership, change of mandate, new banking relationship or material change of corporate purpose, with documented audit trail retained for five years under Article L.561-12 CMF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by INPI, with name-availability verification conducted against the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and the INPI national trademark database; Infogreffe is used as a supplementary watch tool for pre-existing commercial-registry registrations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) may contain words in any language provided they are transliterated in Latin script and do not mislead as to the corporate object or legal form; the SARL legal suffix must appear in French as SARL or Société à Responsabilité Limitée (Article L.223-1 Code de commerce). The name must be lawful, distinctive, and not contrary to public order, and must not imply regulated activities outside the corporate object. French is compulsory for mandatory work contracts, invoices, customs documentation and labelling under the Loi Toubon of 4 August 1994, and the French text prevails for all French-regulatory filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Step 1 — Upon registrar rejection, obtain the written statement of reasons from the INPI RNE controller within 5 business days. Step 2 — Submit a formal administrative review request (réclamation préalable) to INPI within 15 days, proposing either a justification that the name is distinctive and lawful or an amendment to the proposed name. Step 3 — If the administrative review is denied, file a judicial motion before the President of the tribunal judiciaire or tribunal de commerce in the department of the registered office (référé contre le refus de l'INPI) within one month of the refusal letter under Article L.123-6 Code de commerce. Step 4 — Where the rejection arises from an earlier identical or confusingly similar name or trademark, either secure written coexistence consent from the prior right holder or amend the conflicting token and re-file the entire incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique within the remaining 30-day validity window. Step 5 — No fee-shifting applies; the appellant bears court tax and representation costs unless a court order allocates costs differently.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Administratively permitted solely for the siège social through a préfecture-licensed business domiciliation provider (Article L.123-11-1 Code de commerce). However, for ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510 parcel-consolidation and direct-injection linehaul operations, the DGFIP and URSSAF expect a physical operating address (sorting floor, consolidation warehouse, linehaul dispatch point) and an identifiable customs establishment; a pure virtual office would undermine French tax-residency substance and EU customs representation. Virtual office is therefore acceptable only as a complementary administrative seat alongside a dedicated French operating facility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual probability of an unannounced on-site visit of approximately 12%: DGFIP tax-control visits and URSSAF social inspections are unannounced and commonly target newly registered SARLs in transport and logistics; the French customs administration (Douanes) may additionally conduct spot physical checks of the sorting floor and temporary-storage records, adding up to an estimated 5% probability of a customs floor inspection in the first operating year.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Ministry of Economy and Finance; taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr / impots.gouv.fr/pro. Customs and indirect duties authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI); portal: douane.gouv.fr and pro.douane.gouv.fr (DELTA export filing). Large-entity file handling: Direction des Grandes Entreprises (DGE) when applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French-incorporated SARL (subsidiary of foreign parent): (1) incorporation - execute statuts, appoint gérant, deposit share capital (no legal minimum under French law; EUR 1 acceptable), obtain registered-office proof and beneficial-ownership (RBE) details; (2) registration with the Guichet Unique operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) - file statutory incorporation forms (M-description), statuts, manager acceptance, domiciliation agreement, identity documents and RBE declaration; INSEE then allocates the SIREN (9-digit) and SIRET (14-digit) identifiers and the RCS K-bis extract is issued; (3) VAT identification - DGFiP automatically attributes the French intra-Community VAT identifier (format FR + 2-digit key + SIREN) upon RCS registration; the number is retrievable through the professional portal; (4) For a foreign entity registering a French fixed establishment/branch (non-SARL), Form 81032 is filed with the competent SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) to obtain the VAT ID; (5) Non-EU-established foreign principals carrying on taxable French supplies without an EU establishment must appoint a fiscal representative and may be required to post a VAT guarantee (Article 302-2 CGI); the SARL itself being French-established needs no fiscal representative; (6) Customs/export registration for DAE/DAU filing via DELTA (pro.douane.gouv.fr) with appointment of an EORI number (FR + SIREN) if any customs operations are performed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - SARL is by default subject to French corporate income tax (Article 206-1 CGI); territoriality principle applies so only profits attributable to French operations are taxable (Article 209-I CGI); small-SARL pass-through (IR) election is available under Article 239 bis AA CGI (conditions: fewer than 50 employees and turnover or balance sheet total below EUR 10 million); the entity is a French tax resident with unlimited liability for French-sourced income and limits French-source taxation on foreign activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not apply a US-style check-the-box regime; entity classification is statutory. Available elections: (i) Article 239 bis AA CGI - small SARL option to be taxed as a partnership (pass-through to members) for a 5-year irrevocable renewable period, subject to the 50-employee/EUR 10-million tests; (ii) Article 223 A CGI - election to form a French tax group (intégration fiscale) where the French parent holds at least 95% of the SARL; the group files a single corporate tax return; (iii) Article 256 C bis CGI - VAT group election (assujettissement unique à la TVA) for closely linked French entities, effective from 2023; (iv) Article 206-3 CGI - election by partnerships to be subject to corporate tax instead of pass-through. Hybrid and reverse-hybrid mismatches are not elective: Article 212 bis CGI (ATAD 2/BEPS Action 2) applies automatically, imposes deduction denials/income inclusions, and requires disclosure on Form 2257-SD.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) acting in coordination with the European Central Bank and the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under a fully liberalised capital and current account framework pursuant to the EU Treaty and the French Monetary and Financial Code. The euro is fully convertible; no exchange control licences are required for profit remittance, dividend distribution, or loan repayments. Hurdles are limited to tax formalities (withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest or royalties), substance/beneficial-ownership documentation, and anti-money laundering verification that delays bank processing rather than convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory obligation exists to surrender export proceeds or repatriate them within any prescribed timeline. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency in a permitted foreign currency account. A monthly balance-of-payments reporting declaration is required for cross-border transactions exceeding €750,000 (or equivalent) per month under Banque de France regulation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Treasury Account
Operational Account with FX and Trade Finance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Banking (Crédit Agricole CIB)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for EU-licensed EMIs holding an ACPR or EEA passport under PSD2 (e.g., Airwallex, Qonto, Lydia); Low for offshore EMIs without French or EU authorisation. Legal constraint: a payment institution providing services in France must be licensed or passported; unlicensed offshore EMIs are prohibited from operating and may trigger correspondent bank restrictions and ACPR enforcement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted under French AML/CTF rules when using certified video-identification and electronic signature solutions compliant with ACPR guidance; however, for SARLs with non-resident directors or significant cross-border traffic, French commercial banks commonly impose an in-person meeting at a bank branch and require apostilled corporate documents, original banking references, and certified KYC/UBO declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border e-commerce payment traffic inconsistent with declared parcel business scope
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction volume forecast, logistics and carrier contracts, customs broker agreements, warehouse lease, supplier invoices, and the SARL's audited or management financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors, shareholders, or layered beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificat de résidence fiscale (tax residence certificate) of each beneficial owner, corporate registry extracts (Kbis), notarised shareholder register, apostilled trust/ownership deeds, and a transparent org chart of ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mix of client funds and operational treasury float
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standard treasury policy, segregation of entrusted funds, client money accounts if applicable, audited reconciliations, and signed client agreements prohibiting commingling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual purpose codes, lack of economic substance, or unexplained third-party dealings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts and invoices, payroll proof, French office or warehouse lease, local licence evidence (where applicable), and a narrative business plan demonstrating physical presence and operational activity in France.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection must be executed via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit transfer in EUR from the shareholder or parent company. The purpose code must be declared as direct investment (e.g., French balance-of-payments code S1301/1302) or equity injection. The bank requires a notarised shareholder resolution or capital subscription deed, source-of-funds documentation, UBO identification, and proof of tax compliance. No prior exchange control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements use SEPA Instant or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated payments within the eurozone; SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR supplier payments and international disbursements; commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT707) for high-value or documentary trade transactions; B2B direct debit mandates for recurring logistics and carrier settlements. Monthly balance-of-payments reporting is required for aggregate cross-border transactions exceeding €750,000 per month.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (deliverable) for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNY
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to capital controls, executed with eligible ISDA/EMIR-compliant counterparties
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
Plain vanilla FX options to hedge contingent parcel linehaul and cross-border tariff exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March each year for the previous fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €7,500; non-filing may result in administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March each year with updates within 30 days of changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €7,500; persistent non-compliance may trigger administrative sanctions including strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if annual turnover exceeds €800,000 or total assets exceed €400,000

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual DBE filing to DGFiP; updates required within 30 days of shareholding or UBO changes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.00% standard corporate income tax (CIT) rate on all profits of a French tax-resident SARL; reduced rate of 15.00% applies to the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit where the SME ownership and turnover tests are satisfied, with the excess taxed at 25.00%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday or sectoral exemption for parcel consolidation activities. Preferential levers available: research tax credit (CIR) and patent box for qualifying software/IP are not applicable to the declared non-IP hub scope; apprenticeship tax credit and territorial employment aids may reduce effective cash tax marginally; dividend distributions remain subject to shareholder-level French withholding tax or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief; loss carryforward is available under the statutory cap described in this schema.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa No. 2065-SD (core CIT declaration) together with the liasse fiscale annexes 2050 through 2059-G; mandatory electronic filing via the EFI/EDI-TDFC professional portal on impots.gouv.fr; quarterly CIT prepayments are remitted through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with quarterly advance payments (acomptes); for a calendar-year SARL, prepayments are due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, and the balancing settlement is filed with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the annual return must be filed by the second working day immediately following 1 May; for any other fiscal year-end, the return is due within three months of the closing date; the first return of a newly created SARL is prorated from incorporation to the chosen closing date and filed within three months of that closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the statutory accounting year start of the French registered SARL; no special non-resident column exists, as the SARL is a domestic taxpayer.
Insert the French accounting closing date; shareholders do not convert dates to their own residence country.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of months covered by the fiscal year (12 for a standard period).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a short first period, indicate the actual months from incorporation to closing; this proportionally affects the EUR 42,500 reduced-rate band.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit determined under French GAAP (PCG) after tax restatements and all intra-group adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL reports both French and foreign-source income except where the territoriality principle (Article 209 CGI) excludes profits of a genuine foreign branch; attach a reconciliation schedule of accounting-to-tax result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating loss of the current period available for carryforward or carryback election.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Elect carryback (Article 220 quinquies CGI) against the preceding year's taxable profit within the statutory window if cash recovery is preferable to carryforward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of prior-year tax losses against current profit; annual absorption cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess above that amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the cap in the French entity only; do not consolidate with the foreign parent's losses unless a French tax consolidation group has been formally constituted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of CIT at the 15.00% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of profit and at 25.00% on the excess.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the SME conditions (paid-in capital, independence from the foreign parent, ownership structure, turnover ceiling); non-resident ownership does not automatically bar the reduced rate if the tests are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual transfer pricing declaration and basic documentation checklist attached to the CIT return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for every CIT filer regardless of size; disclose related-party warehousing, linehaul, freight and management-fee transactions and claim simplified safe-harbour thresholds where available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% uplift of the tax due if filed after formal notice, 40% for intentional bad faith and 80% for abuse of law or fraudulent maneuvering; late payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month; failure to file Form 2257-SD or to produce transfer pricing documentation triggers the specific TP penalty equal to 5% of the recharacterized adjustment with a EUR 10,000 minimum per fiscal year; missing CbC reporting in a EUR 750M+ group carries a EUR 100,000 maximum administrative fine.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25.00% withholding tax on dividends distributed by a French SARL to non-resident corporations (Article 119 bis (2) CGI); non-resident individuals are subject to the aggregate 30.00% flat levy comprising 12.80% withholding plus 17.20% social levies unless exempt by treaty or EU coordination; the full 25.00% rate is dispensed in favor of EU/EEA corporate parents satisfying the Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The foreign parent must obtain an original or apostilled certificate of tax residence (TRC) from its own competent authority and submit it, together with a completed Form 5001-SD (or the applicable 5000/5003 series form), to the French paying agent before the dividend payment date so that the treaty rate can be applied at source; without a TRC, the full 25.00% statutory rate is withheld and the excess may only be recovered through the ordinary tax refund procedure; EU/EEA parent relief additionally requires a 10% shareholding or voting interest, a minimum unbroken 24-month holding period, and real economic substance of the parent to rebut the CJEU abuse doctrine (Danish Cases C-116/16 and C-117/16).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% statutory withholding on arm's-length commercial third-party debt (Article 119 quater CGI); interest recharacterized as a constructive distribution to a controlling non-resident shareholder (Article 119 bis (1) CGI) carries the 25.00% WHT; treaty rates for genuine debt generally range 0% to 15%, with 0% available within the EU Interest & Royalties Directive. Royalties: statutory 33.33% withholding on licence, patent and copyright sums deemed sourced in France (Article 182 B bis CGI); EU beneficial owners may claim 0% under the Interest & Royalties Directive; otherwise treaty rates of 5% to 10% typically apply; payments to non-cooperative states (ETNC) are subject to the heightened rate, deduction denial and extended statute of limitations.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 gross turnover or gross balance-sheet total triggers the mandatory preparation of a full Local File and Master File (Article L13 AA LPF); groups whose consolidated worldwide revenue equals or exceeds EUR 750,000,000 must additionally file Country-by-Country reporting via Form 2258-SD; every French CIT filer, regardless of size, must submit the simplified Form 2257-SD transfer pricing declaration and maintain adequate contemporaneous evidence of its intercompany pricing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute; substance is nonetheless a hard precondition embedded in the general abuse-of-law rule (Article L64 LPF), Article 155 A CGI on transfer of income to foreigners, the EU ATAD general anti-abuse clause, and treaty anti-abuse jurisprudence (PE, beneficial ownership, Limitation on Benefits). A parcel consolidation hub is treated as a French tax resident because its effective management, warehouse employees and linehaul contracting are physical in France; if substance is hollowed out, the tax administration may disregard the entity, reattribute profits to the foreign parent, deny EU directive or treaty benefits, and apply the 80% abuse-of-law penalty. The hub must therefore maintain genuine payroll, lease, banking, and operational records evidencing real sorting and injection activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Concealment of Revenue (CGI Articles 1729 b and 1741)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or understatement of parcel consolidation and linehaul fees, operation through unreported shadow cash accounts, or failure to file the 2065-SD annual return after one full year of commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil uplift of 40% of the avoided tax for intentional bad faith or 80% for fraudulent maneuvering; criminal fine of EUR 500,000 and up to 5 years imprisonment for simple tax fraud; aggravated fraud involving organized, complex or cross-border schemes carries up to EUR 3,000,000 fine and 7 years imprisonment; late-payment interest of 0.20% per month and court-ordered publication of the judgment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be held personally liable for the company's tax debt under Article L223-22 of the French Commercial Code where the omission results from faute de gestion, with civil restitution of the unpaid taxes and penalties; in aggravated cases the director faces criminal conviction, asset seizure, exit/travel prohibitions, and imprisonment up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Hidden Profit Extraction (CGI Article 57)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging below-market intercompany linehaul or warehousing fees to a related foreign party, paying for non-rendered management services, or concentrating all residual profit in the foreign parent while the French hub bears the operational risk and costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the French taxable base, denial of deduction of the non-arm's-length expenses, upward adjustment of profit, 0.20% monthly interest, 40% penalty for deliberate mispricing, and a specific documentation penalty of 5% of the primary adjustment with a EUR 10,000 minimum per fiscal year; the statute of limitations extends to 12 years for transactions with entities located in non-cooperative states.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign abusive intra-group agreements can be judicially ordered to contribute personal funds to the shortfall under the comblement de passif action; repeated misconduct triggers disqualification from management, travel bans in cross-border collection, and criminal liability where the pricing arrangements are used to conceal fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Law and Sham Shell Structure (Article L64 LPF)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering the SARL as a tax-resident parcel hub with no French warehouse personnel, no local management, no genuine sorting operations, or using circular paper intercompany arrangements solely to attract treaty protection or to capture French-source profits in a low-tax foreign entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The administration disregards the artificial steps, re-files the tax base in the true beneficial owner's hands, imposes the 80% abuse-of-law penalty on the avoided tax, and recovers the underlying withholding tax at source with interest; disclosure obligations and extended assessment windows compound the exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil where substance is fictitious, the gérant is held jointly and severally liable for the reinstated tax and 80% penalties, professional disqualification of up to 15 years may be ordered, travel bans and asset-freezing injunctions are available, and imprisonment up to 5 years applies if the sham is part of an intentional evasion scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Payment Services and AML Non-Compliance (Monetary and Financial Code)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The parcel hub, although not requiring a statutory logistics license, intercepting, pooling or settling customer parcel payments without the authorization required for payment services, bypassing the KYC/KYB controls of Airwallex and local clearing rails, or failing to report suspicious transactions to TRACFIN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Illegal exercise of payment services is a criminal offense punishable by up to 7 years imprisonment and a EUR 750,000 fine, together with confiscation of the related funds; AML violations trigger administrative fines set by the ACPR, prohibition of activity, and mandatory reporting sanctions; intermingling of customer funds with corporate treasury constitutes embezzlement under criminal law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who design or tolerate the unlicensed settlement flow face the same criminal penalties, personal civil restitution to affected customers, preventive attachment of personal assets, professional disqualification, and cross-border travel restrictions pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion on Dividend Repatriation (CGI Articles 119 bis and 119 ter)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to the foreign parent without applying the 25.00% French withholding tax, relying on an expired or false TRC, structuring distributions to a shell intermediary with no beneficial ownership, or claiming the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption without the required 24-month holding period and substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the unpaid withholding tax, 40% bad-faith penalty, 0.20% monthly late interest, and refusal of the directive exemption with retroactive effect; the paying SARL is treated as the withholding agent and bears primary liability for the uncollected amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who signs the general meeting distribution resolution and executes the payment is personally liable for the un-withheld tax under the Commercial Code; criminal prosecution for evasion of source-state tax may attach where the distribution was deliberately disguised, leading to civil restitution, travel bans and imprisonment.
